result.markdown: --- title: "Session 1 — Causal Questions and DAGs" subtitle: "Association vs causation · potential outcomes · confounder, mediator, collider · adjustment sets · Lab 1" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Prediction (A8) asked **who** is at risk. Today: **what would happen if we intervened?** - By the end you can: - state a **causal question** and the **estimand** - draw a **DAG** and name **confounders, mediators, colliders** - let the DAG choose the **adjustment set** ::: ## Our question: did the programme lower blood pressure? ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} - **3,000 adults with hypertension** from routine clinic records (synthetic) - **1,229 (41%) enrolled** in a community health-worker **programme**: **not randomised** - Outcome: **SBP at 12 months** - Also recorded: age, sex, education, urban, BMI, diabetes, **baseline SBP**, **adherence** at 6 months, **clinic visits** in the year ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} htn |> select(age, diabetes, baseline_sbp, programme, adherent, clinic_visits, sbp_12m) |> head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 age diabetes baseline_sbp programme adherent clinic_visits sbp_12m 1 46 0 146 1 0 5 145 2 62 0 138 0 1 5 134 3 63 1 157 0 0 2 171 4 55 0 170 1 0 7 155 5 60 0 173 1 0 2 152 6 57 0 162 0 1 4 155 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Topic 1 — The naive comparison {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Enrolled vs not enrolled ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} htn |> group_by(programme) |> summarise(n = n(), sbp_12m = round(mean(sbp_12m), 1), age = round(mean(age), 1), baseline_sbp = round(mean(baseline_sbp), 1), diabetes = round(mean(diabetes), 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 6 programme n sbp_12m age baseline_sbp diabetes 1 0 1771 143. 53.2 150. 0.13 2 1 1229 142 57.8 157. 0.25 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} SBP at 12 months is **142 vs 143**: a difference of **−1.4 mmHg**. "The programme hardly works"? But the enrolled were **older**, had a **higher baseline SBP (157 vs 150)** and **more diabetes (25% vs 13%)**. Sicker people enrol: **confounding by indication**. The groups were **never comparable**. ::: ## Potential outcomes ::: {.eq} Y¹ = SBP if enrolled Y⁰ = SBP if not enrolled effect for one person = Y¹ − Y⁰ ::: ::: {.incremental} - We only ever see **one** of the two for each person: the **fundamental problem** of causal inference - **ATE** = average of Y¹ − Y⁰ over **everybody** (what if all enrolled vs none?) - **ATT** = average over **those who enrolled** (did it help them?) - A **randomised trial** makes the groups exchangeable. In observational data we need **assumptions**: **no unmeasured confounding** (exchangeability given covariates), **positivity** (everyone could get either option), **consistency** (a well-defined intervention) ::: # Topic 2 — DAGs {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Three roles a variable can play | Role | Structure | Adjust? | |---|---|---| | **Confounder** | C → exposure and C → outcome | **Yes**: closes a back-door path | | **Mediator** | exposure → M → outcome | **No** for the total effect (it removes part of the effect) | | **Collider** | exposure → K ← outcome | **No**: adjusting **opens** a biasing path | ::: {.key} Here: **baseline SBP, age, diabetes, education** are confounders; **adherence** is a **mediator** (the programme works partly by improving adherence); **clinic visits** are a **collider** (the programme brings people in, and so does poor BP). ::: ## The DAG in R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g <- dagitty("dag { programme -> sbp_12m ; programme -> adherent -> sbp_12m programme -> clinic_visits ; sbp_12m -> clinic_visits age -> programme ; age -> sbp_12m ; diabetes -> programme ; diabetes -> sbp_12m baseline_sbp -> programme ; baseline_sbp -> sbp_12m education -> programme ; education -> sbp_12m ; education -> adherent urban -> programme ; urban -> bmi ; bmi -> sbp_12m ; bmi -> baseline_sbp ; bmi -> diabetes age -> baseline_sbp ; age -> diabetes }") plot(graphLayout(g)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s1_causal_questions_dags_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ## Let the DAG choose ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} adjustmentSets(g, exposure = "programme", outcome = "sbp_12m", effect = "total") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { age, baseline_sbp, bmi, diabetes, education } { age, baseline_sbp, diabetes, education, urban } ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} descendants(g, "programme") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "programme" "sbp_12m" "clinic_visits" "adherent" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Two **minimal sufficient sets**: {age, baseline SBP, BMI, diabetes, education} or {age, baseline SBP, diabetes, education, urban} - **Never** adjust for **descendants** of the exposure (adherent, clinic_visits) when you want the **total** effect - The DAG encodes **assumptions**, mostly the **arrows you left out**; the data cannot prove it. Draw it **before** the analysis, from subject knowledge ::: ## What a DAG does not do ::: {.warn} - It cannot show **unmeasured** confounders you did not think of (here an unrecorded "motivation" exists) - It says **what** to adjust for, not **how** (functional form, interactions: A6) - Selecting covariates by **p-values** or stepwise methods is **not** a causal strategy ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 1 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `causal-workshop/labs/lab1_dag.R` - the naive comparison and baseline imbalance - write the DAG with `dagitty` - adjustment sets, paths, descendants ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z1q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="1dr2u6.s7vt64" data-show="VGhlIGdyb3VwcyBkaWZmZXJlZCBiZWZvcmUgdGhlIHByb2dyYW1tZSwgc28gb3V0Y29tZXMg d291bGQgZGlmZmVyIGFueXdheQ==" data-explain="QmFzZWxpbmUgZGlmZmVyZW5jZXMgdGhhdCBhbHNvIGFmZmVjdCB0aGUgb3V0Y29tZSBhcmUg Y29uZm91bmRpbmc6IHRoZSBjb21wYXJpc29uIG1peGVzIHRoZSBlZmZlY3Qgb2YgdGhlIHBy b2dyYW1tZSB3aXRoIHRoZSBlZmZlY3Qgb2YgYmVpbmcgc2lja2VyLg=="} Enrolled adults had a higher baseline SBP and more diabetes. Why can the naive difference in 12-month SBP not be read as the effect? - The sample of 3,000 adults is too small to estimate a difference between two means - The groups differed before the programme, so outcomes would differ anyway - The outcome was measured at 12 months and not at the time of enrolment in the programme - The naive difference has a confidence interval, and causal effects do not have one ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z1q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="1drg2w.s7w7ni" data-show="VGhlIG1lYW4gZGlmZmVyZW5jZSBpZiBldmVyeWJvZHkgd2VyZSBlbnJvbGxlZCB2ZXJzdXMg bm9ib2R5IGVucm9sbGVk" data-explain="VGhlIEFURSBhdmVyYWdlcyB0aGUgaW5kaXZpZHVhbCBlZmZlY3RzIFkxIC0gWTAgb3ZlciB0 aGUgd2hvbGUgcG9wdWxhdGlvbi4gVGhlIGVmZmVjdCBpbiB0aG9zZSB3aG8gZW5yb2xsZWQg aXMgdGhlIEFUVC4="} What is the average treatment effect (ATE)? - The mean difference between the enrolled and the non-enrolled adults as observed - The mean benefit among the adults who actually enrolled in the programme - The mean difference if everybody were enrolled versus nobody enrolled - The largest effect that is seen in any of the subgroups of the cohort ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z1q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="1drtbm.s7wm4w" data-show="Tm86IGl0IGlzIGEgbWVkaWF0b3IsIGFuZCBhZGp1c3RpbmcgcmVtb3ZlcyBwYXJ0IG9mIHRo ZSBlZmZlY3Q=" data-explain="QSBtZWRpYXRvciBsaWVzIG9uIHRoZSBjYXVzYWwgcGF0aC4gQ29uZGl0aW9uaW5nIG9uIGl0 IGJsb2NrcyB0aGF0IHBhdGggYW5kIGxlYXZlcyB0aGUgZGlyZWN0IGVmZmVjdCBvbmx5Lg=="} Adherence is improved by the programme and lowers SBP. If you want the total effect of the programme, should you adjust for adherence? - Yes: it is a confounder, since it is related to both variables - Yes: adjusting for more variables makes the estimate less biased - No: adherence was measured after baseline, so it carries no information - No: it is a mediator, and adjusting removes part of the effect ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z1q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="1ds6k8.s7x0m6" data-show="QSBiaWFzaW5nIHBhdGggaXMgb3BlbmVkLCBiZWNhdXNlIGNsaW5pYyB2aXNpdHMgYXJlIGEg Y29sbGlkZXI=" data-explain="Q29uZGl0aW9uaW5nIG9uIGEgY29tbW9uIGVmZmVjdCBvZiBleHBvc3VyZSBhbmQgb3V0Y29t ZSBjcmVhdGVzIGFuIGFzc29jaWF0aW9uIGJldHdlZW4gdGhlbSB0aGF0IGlzIG5vdCBjYXVz YWw6IGNvbGxpZGVyIGJpYXMu"} Clinic visits are increased by the programme and by a high SBP. What happens if you adjust for clinic visits? - A biasing path is opened, because clinic visits are a collider - The confounding by baseline SBP is removed more completely than before - Nothing changes, because clinic visits are not a cause of the 12-month SBP - The estimate becomes the direct effect of the programme on blood pressure ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z1q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="1dsjsy.s7xf3k" data-show="U3ViamVjdCBrbm93bGVkZ2UgYWJvdXQgaG93IHRoZSB2YXJpYWJsZXMgYXJpc2UsIHNldCBk b3duIGluIGFkdmFuY2U=" data-explain="QSBEQUcgc3RhdGVzIGNhdXNhbCBhc3N1bXB0aW9ucy4gRGF0YSBzaG93IGFzc29jaWF0aW9u cywgd2hpY2ggY2Fubm90IGRpc3Rpbmd1aXNoIGEgY29uZm91bmRlciBmcm9tIGEgbWVkaWF0 b3Igb3IgYSBjb2xsaWRlci4="} What is the best source for the arrows in a DAG? - The p-values of the associations between the variables found in the data - Subject knowledge about how the variables arise, set down in advance - A stepwise selection procedure applied to all of the measured variables - The correlation matrix of the variables, with a cut-off of 0.3 for an arrow ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Causal question** → estimand (**ATE**, **ATT**) → assumptions - **Confounder**: adjust. **Mediator, collider**: do not (for the total effect) - **DAG first**, from subject knowledge; `adjustmentSets()` - The naive comparison is **confounded by indication** - A DAG cannot reveal **unmeasured** confounders ::: **Next:** Session 2: adjustment, bad controls and standardisation

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
